source_book: Sri Chaitanya — IPE STUDY MATERIAL for Jr. Students, Physics (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring. VSAQ 16 questions (17 entries — vsaq10 splits into (a)/(b)), SAQ 16, LAQ 3 (4 entries — laq3 splits into (a)/(b)), PROBLEM 13 (15 entries — prob6 (i)/(ii), prob13 (a)/(b)); 52 entries in all. The FORMULAE block on scan p.83 (printed p.85, left column) is not indexed. Scan pp.85 and 87 are slightly skewed and the right margin of scan p.85 clips two words of SAQ 2; every question was readable. Stems are restated in our own wording with the physics exact; no solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy.

questions.stem: A donkey and a squirrel are each to be given a velocity so that both escape the gravitational field of the earth. What velocity must be given to each of them?
The earth continuously pulls the moon towards its centre. Why does the moon not fall onto the earth?
How much energy does a satellite need in order to keep orbiting (air resistance neglected)? Justify the answer.
If the gravitational force on a body is proportional to its mass, why does a heavy body not fall faster than a lighter body?
Statement: when an apple falls towards the earth, the earth also moves up to meet the apple. Is this statement true or false? Justify the answer.
Why does an astronaut in a satellite revolving around the earth feel weightless?
Hydrogen escapes from the surface of the earth faster than oxygen does. Why?
Two masses of 20 kg and 30 kg are placed 5 m apart. Find the gravitational force of attraction between them.
A satellite of mass 1000 kg revolves at a height of 500 km above the surface of the earth. Calculate the potential energy of the satellite.
questions.notes: The question prints no value for G, the mass of the earth or the radius of the earth; standard values must be assumed.

questions.stem: A nut becomes loose and gets detached from a satellite revolving around the earth. Will the nut fall down to the earth, or will it revolve around the earth? Give reasons for the answer.
The weight of an object is more at the poles than at the equator. At which of these two places do we get more sugar for the same weight? State the reason for the answer.
It is safe to jump from a height of 2 m on the earth. Calculate the safe jumping height on a planet where g = 1.96 m/s².
questions.notes: The value of g on the earth is not printed in the question; the standard 9.8 m/s² must be assumed.
